Scarlett O'Hara corresponds to Cheng Yanxiu: These two characters are the heroines in "Gone with the Wind" and "The Peony Pavilion", respectively. Their destiny and emotions are the core of the works.

Serena O'Hara corresponds to Zhong Kui: This analogy may not be appropriate. Serena O'Hara is a character in "Gone with the Wind", she is Scarlett's mother. Zhong Kui is a theatrical character in "The Peony Pavilion", and there is no obvious analogy between him and Serena.

Lark Hamp corresponds to Han Yu: This analogy may also not be appropriate. Lark Hamp is a character in "Gone with the Wind", one of Scarlett's lovers. Han Yu is a historical figure in "The Peony Pavilion", who played the role of a minister giving advice. The two characters have significant differences in status and personality in the works.

background.source: Gone with the Wind is a timeless classic that has touched the hearts of millions of people around the world. Written by Margaret Mitchell in 1936, the novel tells the story of Scarlett O'Hara, a self-centered Southern belle living in Georgia during the Civil War. Scarlett is headstrong and determined, and through her trials and tribulations, she learns the endurance and resilience that is required to survive in a world torn apart by war. Alongside Scarlett are other important characters like her sisters, Serena and Lark, who also experience the hardships of living in the South during this tumultuous time in history. In 1939, the novel was adapted into a film of the same name, which went on to become one of the most beloved movies in history. The film starred Vivien Leigh as Scarlett O'Hara, and was a stunning visual masterpiece with a sweeping score and lavish costumes. With its rich and complex characters, stunning plot, and powerful themes, Gone with the Wind will always hold a special place in the hearts of readers and moviegoers alike.
background.target: The Peach Blossom Fan is a renowned musical play and historical drama written by Kong Shangren during the early Qing dynasty. The play, with 44 scenes, took more than a decade to complete and tells the story of the collapse of the Ming dynasty through the love story of its two main characters, scholar Hou Fangyu and courtesan Li Xiangjun. It is considered one of China's greatest historical dramas and explores themes of power, love, and sacrifice. The English translation, completed by Chen Shih-hsiang, Harold Acton, and Cyril Birch, enables non-Chinese speakers to appreciate its beauty and significance fully. While the play is not directly related to Tang Xianzu, Cheng Yanxiu, Zhong Kui, and Han Yu, they are all notable figures in traditional Chinese literature and have inspired many works, including The Peach Blossom Fan.
